evidence: The surviving solution explicitly uses "Exact cover with dancing links" and creates "columns: bases ..., catalysts ..., essences ...".
affordance_in_statement: A successful Grand Synthesis requires that you choose exactly k recipes such that every base liquid, rare catalyst, and elemental essence is consumed in exactly one chosen recipe.
removal_suggestion: No safe rewording removes this affordance without changing the core task: the problem is intrinsically an exact-cover/3-dimensional matching instance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Models the requirement directly as an exact-cover instance and solves it with dancing links.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Choose exactly k recipes while using every item in each of the three ingredient sets exactly once.

common_affordance: The requirement is an exact cover of three disjoint sets by the explicitly listed recipe triples.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It stores recipes in a dictionary keyed only by (base, catalyst), so multiple valid recipes sharing those two ingredients overwrite one another; its 2^(2k)-scale DP representation is also impractical at k=22.
It falls back to brute-force/backtracking-style search for a 3-dimensional matching and exceeds the time limit on hard instances.
Its compressed DP retains only one essence-mask representative for a state, discarding alternative partial selections that can lead to different valid completions.

recommended_edit: Make no edit: the only shared surviving approach exploits the intrinsic structure of the required exact cover, and removing it would change the problem rather than eliminate a wording-based shortcut.
